blocks.text:
# pr-1765: gh-1745 [PERF] Marathon session files grow to 1GB due to unrotated model_request_summary raw prompt dumps

## Description

Closes #1745
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745
```

<details><summary>Record flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  EVT[ModelRequestEvent] --> STORE[TrajectoryRequestBlobStore]
  STORE -->|full detail + wire dump| BLOB[".fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json"]
  STORE -->|strip| REC["model_request_summary: sizes, hashes, spillFile"]
  REC --> JSONL[session .jsonl — lightweight]
  BLOB --> ROT["TTL 30d · 50MB/session · newest kept"]
```
</details>

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper.     "description": "Closes #1745
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

```bash
dart test test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. ### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vi-` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:8`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vod` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:129`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vsc` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:1453`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart` line 183

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` line 1453

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

    "description": "Closes #1745
### What changed
- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.

- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.

# Session Delta — What Changed Since Your Last Leg

- **Mode**: `FIRST-LEG`
- **HEAD SHA**: `none` → `700976938c38f09cd45905b7338e979d60b777f9` *(unchanged)*

## Input Files (`input/<ticket>/`)

- **NEW** (9): `ci_failures.md`, `pr_diff.txt`, `pr_discussions.md`, `pr_discussions_raw.json`, `pr_info.md`, `review_state.md`, `rework_base_head.txt`, `ticket.json`, `ticket.md`

- **UNCHANGED** (0): _none_

## New Comments & Review Threads (29)

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — **unknown** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart:297`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) renders `message.preview` — now always `''` for new sessions — and `message.blocks` — now absent — with no `spillFile` row. `grep spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only the writer side.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:147` renders `'…: ${message.preview…}'` → spilled sessions export as `role · N chars: ` with a dangling colon.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), or scope this PR to the CLI host until the app viewer exists.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vi-` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:8`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vod` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:129`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vsc` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:1453`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

### 6. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_a4R` — **unknown** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart:299`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, still valid on this head): spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

This hunk wires spilling into the app host and stubs the buffered detail to role+chars (`preview: ''`, no blocks, `spillFile` pointer), but the app-side readers were not updated:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` `_requestPage` renders `message.preview` (now always `''` for every new session) and `message.blocks` (now always empty) — with no `spillFile` row and no blob resolution. Verified: `grep -rn spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only this writer side.

  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart` line 297

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) renders `message.preview` — now always `''` for new sessions — and `message.blocks` — now absent — with no `spillFile` row. `grep spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only the writer side.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:147` renders `'…: ${message.preview…}'` → spilled sessions export as `role · N chars: ` with a dangling colon.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), or scope this PR to the CLI host until the app viewer exists.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart` line 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart` line 183

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` line 129

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` line 1453

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

---

### Thread 7 — `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart` line 299

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, still valid on this head): spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

This hunk wires spilling into the app host and stubs the buffered detail to role+chars (`preview: ''`, no blocks, `spillFile` pointer), but the app-side readers were not updated:

name: fa_ui
description: >-
  Reusable UI for apps embedding the Fa agent: the Fa brand theme (dark +
  light, customizable via FaUiTheme), and ready-made provider/model settings
  widgets (provider presets, custom-provider registry, media model slots)
  with host-overridable strings.
version: 0.0.1
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2
  flutter: ">=1.17.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core): ExecutionEnv
  # for the persisted stores, AgentConfig for the connect flow, and the
  # shared /models endpoint parser.
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../../

  # ChatTheme for the flutter_chat_ui theme builders.
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0

  # The chat transcript UI (chat/): markdown rendering and the chat surface.
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media (chat/media_player.dart):
  # audio plays from in-memory bytes, video from a temp file staged via
  # path_provider (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0
  path_provider: ^2.1.6

  # The /models endpoint fetch behind the model quick select.
  http: ^1.6.0

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — **unknown** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart:297`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) renders `message.preview` — now always `''` for new sessions — and `message.blocks` — now absent — with no `spillFile` row. `grep spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only the writer side.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:147` renders `'…: ${message.preview…}'` → spilled sessions export as `role · N chars: ` with a dangling colon.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file

- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.

## New Comments & Review Threads (29)

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — **unknown** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart:297`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) renders `message.preview` — now always `''` for new sessions — and `message.blocks` — now absent — with no `spillFile` row. `grep spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only the writer side.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:147` renders `'…: ${message.preview…}'` → spilled sessions export as `role · N chars: ` with a dangling colon.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), or scope this PR to the CLI host until the app viewer exists.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vi-` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:8`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vod` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:129`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vsc` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:1453`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200

  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`

- `model_request_summary` records no longer carry their heavy payloads: per-message previews/block texts and the opt-in raw wire dump spill to `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/<n>.json`; the primary session JSONL keeps lightweight metadata (counts, sizes, tool names, blob hashes) plus a `spillFile` pointer.
- New `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore` (pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv`) writes + rotates the blobs: 50 MB/session, 30-day TTL, oldest-first with the newest always kept; wired into both persist hosts (CLI + app service). `/trajectory inspect` names the blob.

### Key decisions
- Default ON; `trajectory.requestBlobs: false` (+ `requestBlobMaxMb`, `requestBlobTtlDays`, strict section) restores the legacy inline persistence byte-identically.
- A failed spill write degrades to the legacy inline path — the capture is never lost, never a crash (same shape as tool-result spilling).
- Replay-safe: the usage fold's Σ `messages[].chars` basis survives the stubbing; old sessions render as before; `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073) still bounds the blob payload.

```bash

cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service_test.dart --plain-name gh-1745

name: fa_ui
description: >-
  Reusable UI for apps embedding the Fa agent: the Fa brand theme (dark +
  light, customizable via FaUiTheme), and ready-made provider/model settings
  widgets (provider presets, custom-provider registry, media model slots)
  with host-overridable strings.
version: 0.0.1
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2
  flutter: ">=1.17.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core): ExecutionEnv
  # for the persisted stores, AgentConfig for the connect flow, and the
  # shared /models endpoint parser.
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../../

  # ChatTheme for the flutter_chat_ui theme builders.
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0

  # The chat transcript UI (chat/): markdown rendering and the chat surface.
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media (chat/media_player.dart):
  # audio plays from in-memory bytes, video from a temp file staged via
  # path_provider (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0
  path_provider: ^2.1.6

  # The /models endpoint fetch behind the model quick select.
  http: ^1.6.0

citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — **unknown** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_events.dart:297`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), or scope this PR to the CLI host until the app viewer exists.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vi-` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:8`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vod` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:129`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `TrajectorySection.requestBlobMaxBytes` is dead code — use it**

The getter (`cli_config.dart:129`) is never referenced: both hosts re-derive the byte budget inline —

- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart`: `maxBytes: config.trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_lifecycle.dart`: `maxBytes: trajectoryRequestBlobMaxMb << 20`

Two copies of the MB→bytes shift with the canonical one unused. Either thread `section.requestBlobMaxBytes` through `CliConfig`/`AgentCliConfig` (a `trajectoryRequestBlobMaxBytes` field) so both call sites consume the getter, or drop the getter.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vsc` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:1453`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the config SAVE path (`_trajectoryYaml`) is untested**

The new tests cover parsing (`requestBlobs` defaults, knob validation, strict unknown keys) and `loadProjectTrajectorySection`, but nothing round-trips a save: `_trajectoryYaml()` writes `requestBlobs: false` / non-default knobs only-when-non-default (defaults never written — the file-stays-minimal convention). One assertion like:

```dart
final saved = config.copyWith(trajectoryRequestBlobs: false).toYamlString();
expect(saved, contains('requestBlobs: false'));
```

would pin the save shape (the sibling sections each have one). Low risk — the parse tests would catch a malformed key on the next load — but the asymmetry is free to close.

  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).

name: fa_ui
description: >-
  Reusable UI for apps embedding the Fa agent: the Fa brand theme (dark +
  light, customizable via FaUiTheme), and ready-made provider/model settings
  widgets (provider presets, custom-provider registry, media model slots)
  with host-overridable strings.
version: 0.0.1
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2
  flutter: ">=1.17.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core): ExecutionEnv
  # for the persisted stores, AgentConfig for the connect flow, and the
  # shared /models endpoint parser.
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../../

  # ChatTheme for the flutter_chat_ui theme builders.
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0

  # The chat transcript UI (chat/): markdown rendering and the chat surface.
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media (chat/media_player.dart):
  # audio plays from in-memory bytes, video from a temp file staged via
  # path_provider (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0
  path_provider: ^2.1.6

  # The /models endpoint fetch behind the model quick select.
  http: ^1.6.0

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200

- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer

  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext

blocks.text:
name: fa_ui
description: >-
  Reusable UI for apps embedding the Fa agent: the Fa brand theme (dark +
  light, customizable via FaUiTheme), and ready-made provider/model settings
  widgets (provider presets, custom-provider registry, media model slots)
  with host-overridable strings.
version: 0.0.1
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2
  flutter: ">=1.17.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core): ExecutionEnv
  # for the persisted stores, AgentConfig for the connect flow, and the
  # shared /models endpoint parser.
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../../

  # ChatTheme for the flutter_chat_ui theme builders.
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0

  # The chat transcript UI (chat/): markdown rendering and the chat surface.
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media (chat/media_player.dart):
  # audio plays from in-memory bytes, video from a temp file staged via
  # path_provider (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0
  path_provider: ^2.1.6

  # The /models endpoint fetch behind the model quick select.
  http: ^1.6.0

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

The ticket's Proposed Fix section only describes the `model_request_summary` remediation, so the implementation matches the fix plan — please just confirm the `shell_job_registry` half has a follow-up issue (or extend the blob/TTL policy to it here) so "Closes #1745" doesn't retire the ticket with a quarter of the cited disk growth still open.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — **unknown** (`lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs.dart:183`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vsc` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart:1453`)
